question: What is something you believed for years before finding out it was completely false?
story: For eleven years I believed my grandmother had been a professional wrestler. There was a framed photo in her hallway of a woman in a shiny cape holding a championship belt, and whenever I asked about it she would just smile and say that was a long time ago. That was the entire answer. I built a personality around it. I told teachers. I told dates. In sixth grade I did a family history project called My Grandmother, The Champion, and I got an A on it. Then at her seventieth birthday I stood up and gave a toast about her wrestling career, in front of forty people, holding a microphone. The room went completely silent. Here is what that photo actually was. A five dollar costume booth at a county fair in nineteen seventy one. She let it run for eleven years because, in her words, it was the most attention I ever gave her.
